title: Statistics and quantitative reasoning for law
audience: a pre-law college student (any major) preparing for law school and the LSAT
purpose: Use probability, Bayes' theorem, sampling, confidence intervals, hypothesis tests and regression, and evaluate statistical evidence in litigation and policy, such as disparity statistics, forensic match probabilities and damages estimates.

weeks.4: The prosecutor's fallacy and base rates
weeks.11: Expected value and present value in damages

blocks.deliverable: Summarize a data set and compute conditional probabilities.
Compute the posterior probability for a forensic match.
Build and interpret a confidence interval for a proportion.
Week 7 midterm; test a disparity in hiring rates.
Interpret a regression table and name two confounders.
Compute expected damages and the present value of a lost-earnings claim.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Expert-report critique: analyze a supplied statistical report written for the course in an employment-discrimination case, recompute its key numbers, and write a 1,200-word memo on its strengths and weaknesses.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.

files.L04.txt: The prosecutor's fallacy and base rates
files.L11.txt: Expected value and present value in damages
